investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent 'BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 (+https://github.com/chriswatson6675/band_on_the_map)', no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official /programmation/ page, homepage, and one event detail page. The programmation page carries NO schema.org JSON-LD Event data (0 <script type=application/ld+json> blocks) — every field comes from the page's own repeated static 'gt-event-listing' (WordPress 'eventchamp' theme) card markup, which already states title+full date (day+month name+4-digit year)+time+event URL directly per card. Fully answered at Level 1, no escalation needed.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the official programmation page (https://www.cafedeladanse.com/programmation/) found a WordPress site running the 'eventchamp' theme (wp-theme-eventchamp / eventchamp-theme markup) with NO JSON-LD Event data at all, but whose own repeated static 'gt-event-listing' card markup directly states, per event: a full French-language date including the 4-digit year (e.g. '5 septembre 2026'), a start time (e.g. '20h00'), the event's own title, and its own canonical /event/{slug}/ URL — 47 raw card matches (35 unique events once a duplicate 'Nouvelles dates !' promotional widget further down the same page is deduplicated by slug). The homepage additionally states the venue's own full postal address directly in its own text. This fully answers the investigation question at Level 1; no structural/browser escalation was needed.

time.notes: Each card's own 'gt-time' text (e.g. '19h00'), stated directly. No timezone offset is stated anywhere sampled — recorded honestly as FLOATING_LOCAL, never upgraded to a UTC instant.

venue_location.notes: Single-venue source: every event belongs to this one venue. The venue's own retained homepage states '05 Passage Louis-Philippe 75011 Paris' directly in its own page text — an exact match to this task's assigned address. The listing page itself does not repeat the address per card (single-venue convention, matching Badehaus Berlin/silent green precedent: resolved by source_id, not re-stated per event).

source_record_id.notes: No numeric id is exposed on the card itself. Each card's own href is this source's own permanent '/event/{slug}/' WordPress permalink page, so the slug is used as source_record_id — the same documented judgement already accepted for badehaus-berlin/tempodrom-berlin/silent-green-kulturquartier-berlin (a permalink URL slug the source uses as its own canonical path). Not independently re-verified by a second live fetch within this investigation's bounded scope, but WordPress permalink slugs are a well-established stable platform convention, not a value this investigation invented.

event_url.notes: Each card's own href, stated directly.

price.notes: No price value is ever printed on a card or its own detail page — only a 'TICKET' button/label linking out to one of several third-party ticketing platforms observed across sampled cards (SeeTickets, Weezevent, Ticketmaster, dice.fm), confirming this task's note that ticketing is split across several third parties per event. No first-party price text exists to record.

blockers.description: This page's own markup carries a minority of events (12 of 47 raw card matches, 0 of 35 once deduplicated) TWICE: once in the main chronological listing and again in a separate 'Nouvelles dates !' promotional widget further down the same page, with byte-identical title/date/time. A collector must deduplicate by the event's own URL slug (keeping the first/main-listing occurrence) — implemented and offline-proven in ingestion/cafe-de-la-danse-paris/observation-adapter.mjs's extractEventCards(). Not CRITICAL: the underlying data is genuinely available, this is a housekeeping deduplication step, not a data-availability gap.

Ticketing/price is fully external and split across at least 4 distinct third-party platforms (SeeTickets, Weezevent, Ticketmaster, dice.fm) observed across sampled cards, with no consistent URL shape between them. A future Offer-layer collector wanting per-event ticket/price data would need either per-platform scraping or to leave Offers unpopulated for this source — out of scope for this Observation-layer investigation.
